original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Repair the repeated registered-check workspace failure in half-stage-evacuation and source-partner-residual-exchanges, preserving every mathematical check and explicit retained workspaces.
scope_change_reason: Adopt item 2 of kumagi's released handoff in discussioncomment-18978663. This is replay lifecycle reliability, not a runtime speedup or new mechanism.
bottleneck_link: Repeated source-bound owner and moment checks should not fail because an earlier replay left an ignored work directory. This is verification tooling, not an improvement to the selected supplier.
stop_rule: Finish after both actual registered checks pass twice in the same checkout and lifecycle controls pass. Do not change proof bodies, scientific inputs, source archives, pinned receipts, shared runner or selected record.
evidence: README.md records failing and passing registered commands; verify.py tests the actual CLI entry points, cleanup, interruption, retained diagnostics and existing-path refusal. Its optional --full mode reruns both registered commands twice.

overlap.scope: Open PR titles/bodies including drafts, discussion bodies/comments/replies and local package metadata. Closed work only through local notes/ledger; no code-diff search. PR3009 closes handoff item 1, not this workspace repair. No competing repair found; not a novelty certificate.

open_questions.question: Do these workspace controls and repeated registered checks pass on native Windows?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Temporary-directory cleanup and open-file handling differ across operating systems.
open_questions.first_step: Run python3.12 -B research/owner-replay-workspaces/verify.py --full on Windows; preserve any platform skip and exact interpreter version.
open_questions.blocked_by: This contribution was checked on Linux only. Symlink fixtures require local privileges; an unavailable symlink fixture is reported as a skip, not a pass.
